hook_text: Drop clips on a magnet and they all run to the ends. Then sprinkle iron filings and see the reason.
clip_script: Scatter paper clips over a bar magnet. They pile on the two ends and leave the middle bare. Those ends are the poles, and that is where the pull lives. Hang the magnet on a thread and it swings until one end points north. Call that end N. Bring N up to another magnet's S and they snap together. Flip it, N to N, and feel the push. Unlike poles attract, like poles repel, and only the push proves you have a real magnet, because plain iron never pushes back. Cut a magnet in half and you get two whole magnets, each with N and S. Now slide the magnet under paper and shake on iron filings. Curved lines appear, tight at the ends, loose in the middle. That is the field, and tight lines mean strong pull. That is why the clips chose the ends.
visual_style: Whiteboard bar magnet with clips clustering at the ends; two magnets snapping and repelling; filings forming field lines from N to S.
mood: Playful discovery, each test answering the last question.
pacing: Quick clip pile, swing to north, snap and push, pause on the filings reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and plot a field line with a compass yourself.
